instruction: I want my terminal to have a transparent background so I can see my desktop wallpaper through it. Enable terminal transparency permanently so it persists after system reboot.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(1); pyautogui.write('gsettings get org.gnome.Terminal.Legacy.Profile:/org/gnome/terminal/legacy/profiles:/:$(gsettings get org.gnome.Terminal.ProfilesList default | tr -d "'")/ use-transparent-background'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.press('enter')

metadata.explanation: Task requires permanently enabling terminal transparency. Evaluator opens new terminal and checks use-transparent-background setting using gsettings, expecting 'true'. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric with vm_terminal_output getter.
metadata.similarity_to_original: high - same pattern of OS terminal configuration that persists across reboots

Properly addresses both requirements: enabling transparency AND persistence across reboots (gsettings stores to dconf which persists)

Data flow is correct: vm_terminal_output getter extracts terminal output → check_include_exclude metric checks for 'true' substring → expected value is semantically correct
